briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 29, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Health Emergency
sections.content: Globally, the severity of the climate crisis is escalating, leading to a global health emergency. In the decade since the Paris Agreement, an average of 540,000 people have died annually due to heatwaves [14], and Lancet Countdown reports warn that the health impacts of climate change are accelerating [6, 142, 144, 148, 155]. Direct impacts of climate change are manifesting worldwide, such as the disappearance of glaciers from Slovenia's national flag [2] and seasonal rainfall in central Japan reaching three times the average [143]. Economic damages are also intensifying, with warnings about a climate finance gap as 51 developing countries require $6.9 trillion for climate action [17], and Germany's automotive supply chain is threatened by climate risks [156]. It has been pointed out that the financial sector must capture the full spectrum of these climate change risks [138]. With greenhouse gas concentrations reaching record highs [74], climate change is increasing crop damage [140] and posing significant risks to France's historical heritage [149].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Climate Change Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality Implementation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway for climate change adaptation and carbon neutrality implementation. Gyeongsangbuk-do Province is promoting bluefin tuna farming in response to changes in fish species due to climate change [1], and Haenam-gun is exploring the future of the agricultural sector by hosting events that combine climate change response with robotic technology [3, 4, 5, 9, 13, 20]. Korea Rural Community Corporation aims to enhance flood and drought resilience using AI and digital technologies [11, 12, 16, 19], and the Korea Institute of Energy Research is focusing on developing technology-based solutions, such as an integrated design platform for renewable energy in industrial complexes [134]. Seoul Metropolitan Government has launched its 3rd Climate Crisis Response Committee to deliberate on carbon neutrality policies [26, 33, 61, 71], and Korea East-West Power has set a goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 79% by 2040 [30, 45, 52], thus concretizing reduction targets in the public and industrial sectors. Throughout 2024, 43.6 million tons of carbon were reduced globally through Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology [24, 37], and domestic and international companies are also leading carbon neutrality efforts by joining the UN Global Compact [34] and pursuing sustainable carbon neutrality [161].

sections.title: 🌍 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Challenges of Stable Energy Transition
sections.content: Renewable energy is now transforming the global power market, establishing itself as a key driver of the worldwide energy transition, notably surpassing coal-fired power generation for the first time [129]. Domestically, Hanwha Solutions achieved a third-quarter turnaround to profit, driven by improved profitability in its renewable energy sector [88, 89, 106, 107, 110, 118, 126, 135, 136], emerging as a crucial factor in corporate competitiveness [75]. The Saemangeum region aims for a major transformation into an AI, hydrogen, and RE100 industrial city through its 10GW renewable energy expansion plan [97, 105, 109, 121], and Hampyeong-gun is actively promoting the creation of large-scale regional renewable energy production bases by presenting an RE100 industrial complex vision and accelerating efforts to attract semiconductor companies [104, 115, 131]. However, there are criticisms that related regulations are insufficient compared to the speed of renewable energy deployment [80], and the Korea Power Exchange is facing challenges for a stable energy transition, such as testing grid stability in response to increased renewable energy [99]. Globally, while the expansion of renewable energy capacity is slowing, Energy Storage Systems (ESS) are projected to increase by 45% [96], indicating their crucial role in future energy systems.

sections.title: 📰 International Climate Response Discussions and COP31 Preparations
sections.content: The international community is closely watching the upcoming 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31, and continuing discussions on climate response [151, 152]. Notably, EU officials have stated that the climate finance outlook at COP31 is 'at risk of being stranded' [153], emphasizing the importance of climate finance. China is demonstrating efforts to expand its role, expecting a carbon reduction effect equivalent to Brazil's annual CO2 emissions through clean technology exports in 2026 [163], with experts focusing on what agenda China will pursue at COP31 [162]. Governments worldwide continue to develop climate action plans, such as the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador announcing the development of a new climate change action plan and initiating public engagement [158, 160]. Concurrently, academic achievements that provide insights into modern climate research are consistently being published, including the demonstration of 'oceanic chain reactions' that triggered past ice ages [18] and research on the link between fossil horses in Madrid 9 million years ago and climate change [157].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has once again underscored the severity of the global climate crisis, along with the diverse adaptation and mitigation efforts underway both domestically and internationally, the acceleration of renewable energy transition, and the importance of international cooperation. This is a critical juncture where humanity's wisdom and action for a sustainable future are more urgently needed than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
